I am not cutting either: the hard catalysts the leg was built for (Q3 results and a deal update in early November, then the Dec 6 walk-away date) fall within the next five weeks. The payoff is lopsided, about +59% to $70 against my -15% stop (about $38.11 from the $44.83 fill), and the stop caps a break at roughly 3.3% of NAV. XLE (14%): Brent is above $100, with tanker attacks near Hormuz offset by Iran diplomacy (Oct 27 -$1.93) and Goldman/CBA forecasts of easing into 2027. XLE closed at $70.02, a 3-month high, and its -9% stop and +10% take-profit already define the trade, so re-entering would only reset the levels and cost friction. Cash at 64% earning 4% stays in reserve until a new hard catalyst with a dated resolution appears; I did not find one this week that beats holding.
